question.problem:
Which of the following are elementary matrices?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that an elementary matrix is obtained by performing exactly one elementary row operation on the identity matrix $I.$

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- The matrix $A$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from $I$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-10){R}_{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-10){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =A\end{aligned}
$$

- The matrix $B$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from $I$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:=7{R}_{3},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=7{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

- The matrix $C$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from $I$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-9){R}_{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-9){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $A$, $B$, and $C$ are elementary matrices.
